### 2026-10-31: Finished up the case, used the datasheet from adafruit but I'm sourcing the display from aliexpress since its cheaper.

**0.75h**

Finished up the case, used the datasheet from adafruit but I'm sourcing the display from aliexpress since its cheaper.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/ac03c98a1a3770a42959799a1da7b303604a8aeb8d92ee362830522a11e10a77.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/2deafa1b2ec66517872bdbacecfce250b80858de143f5854566641e7431fadb6.png)

I also worked on the software side of the music player. So the approach I'm going to take is to use EGLFS to display a Qt app fullscreen, which means that I don't need a window manager running, and that would hopefully make it smoother. Originally, I was going to use an SPI connection to the screen but I realised that with the resolution of the screen this would end up being like 4fps max and that's really no good for displaying lyrics.

### 2026-10-31: So I decided to use the "iced" rust crate instead of going the qt route, which means I will have to use some sort of display compositor, and so I chose the "cage" compositor (https://github.com/cage-k

**4h**

So I decided to use the "iced" rust crate instead of going the qt route, which means I will have to use some sort of display compositor, and so I chose the "cage" compositor (https://github.com/cage-kiosk/cage/wiki) which is a very lightweight kiosk mode compositor, meaning it only shows one window. This is perfect for me since my firmware is basically just like any other normal desktop app except I put it in a 800x480 window that cannot be resized, and this will be fullscreen (same resolution as display, and I set the scaling to 1x, using a kiosk mode compositor). Currently for the firmware I just have a test app which can show off the features of the board such as controlling the headphone output amplifier (enable/disable, set to -6/0/3/6 db)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/796334cdc318f8022144cdb3f5a5d9a92cf67ff09fe7625e4aba7eb57aa4a264.png)

I am also testing on my host machine, since obviously I don't have the board yet so I am using wiringpi development mode, which means it prints to the terminal the changes in pin states.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/e4cc4abfb552562ae927550dbf96f864c56fee4d04c66b4c4b04876da1e2a37e.png)

enable and disable amp is very simple, since it is just setting the pin to high or low

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/53d26cabbb04d41ccaf7457a1dd006c5407d2fb64be73186cf16d112ce96e9e2.png)

to control the volume, we must set two pins (g0 and g1) which have four states (2^2) and correspond to the different amplifications. according to the datasheet, 00 is -6db, 10 is +0db, 01 is +3db and 11 is +6db.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/cf97669b019b49f7d729fc9038dfc0f672c21ab3ebacdc527f29e492c5dfc005.png)
